question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

With the 21st Party Congress approaching in late 2027, analysts see no signals of retirement or successor elevation, consistent with his prior abolition of term limits and pattern of extending authority. Traders assign a 95.8% probability he remains in office through 2026, reflecting the absence of organized opposition or public challenges within elite networks. While this consensus rests on observable institutional dominance, sudden health developments, elite fractures during economic stress, or major external shocks could still shift dynamics before the end of 2026.

Traders appear to discount name recognition alone in favor of electability signals and post-midterm dynamics that could accelerate or derail candidacies.

Recent polling shows Kamala Harris often leading nationally, while Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Gavin Newsom, and Jon Ossoff trade momentum in surveys and early-state testing, driven by their national profiles, fundraising networks, and positioning ahead of the 2026 midterms. The Democratic National Committee’s shift to South Carolina and Nevada as the initial contests favors candidates with stronger appeal among diverse voter coalitions. Ossoff’s Senate re-election campaign in Georgia and Ocasio-Cortez’s visibility among progressives have lifted their implied probabilities, while Newsom’s travel to early states and Harris’s established base keep them competitive. Traders appear to discount name recognition alone in favor of electability signals and post-midterm dynamics that could accelerate or derail candidacies.
